title: A Survey of Secure Computation Using Trusted Execution Environments
review_status: full-text audit complete; survey taxonomy and encrypted-query comparison reviewed; not a new controlled DB benchmark
sections_checked: Appendix A encrypted database-query landscape and streaming-data observation
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2023-02-23; full HTML audited
evidence_note: Survey separates outsourced, distributed, and multiparty protocols and compares setting, method, security, and performance. Database-query appendix reports focus on relational SQL and few studies on streaming data, naming a 2019 exception. This is a synthesis, not controlled head-to-head evidence; comparisons inherit heterogeneous underlying setups.

title: Context-based Ontology Modelling for Database: Enabling ChatGPT for Semantic Database Management
review_status: full-text audit complete; two healthcare database case studies support schema-context utility but not broad benchmark transfer
sections_checked: two semantic integration and multi-table join case studies
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2023-03-11; full PDF audited
evidence_note: In illustrated cases, schema context repairs missed field mappings and supplies a missing join path; each of two tasks is repeated ten times. Authors call for larger databases and more complex operations. Two case studies, not a broad benchmark or cross-model replication.

title: Privacy-Preserving Data Management using Blockchains
review_status: full-text audit complete; single-machine latency comparison measured with roughly 38-42 percent overhead for two query classes; security and scale claims remain setup-bounded
sections_checked: privacy tuple and permissioned blockchain architecture
single-machine query evaluation for three data categories
native versus privacy-aware latency and overhead
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2024-08-21; full HTML audited
evidence_note: On one 8-logical-processor, 16-GB machine, demographic query mean is 22.99 ms privacy-aware versus 13.37 ms native (41.85% overhead); healthcare query 21.67 versus 13.38 ms (38.26%). Authors state cross-system performance comparison is impractical because privacy models, infrastructure, and blockchain differ.

title: The Interpretability Analysis of the Model Can Bring Improvements to the Text-to-SQL Task
review_status: full-text audit complete; small WikiSQL gains vary by metric and comparator; single-table task scope and inference-time cost disclosed
sections_checked: processing-time limitation and future complex-query work
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2025-08-12; full PDF audited
evidence_note: CESQL test logical-form/execution accuracy is 87.7/93.0 versus listed SeaD+EG 87.1/92.7; in aggregation comparison CESQL 88.0/93.1 while IESQL+EG+AE has higher logical-form score 87.8 vs 87.7. Authors focus on WikiSQL single-table queries and note added processing time. No evidence here of transfer to complex modern multi-table benchmarks.

title: DriftBench: Defining and Generating Data and Query Workload Drift for Benchmarking
review_status: full-text audit complete; controlled drift generation and census cardinality-estimator case study reviewed; external realism and other component classes unvalidated
sections_checked: PostgreSQL, Naru, and MSCN Q-error under two data variants and six workloads
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2025-10-12; full HTML audited
evidence_note: DriftBench generates parameterized data/workload changes and demonstrates estimator-specific Q-error responses on census-derived variants and six workloads. PostgreSQL average Q-error is relatively stable with outlier pattern changes; Naru shifts on skewed data; MSCN responds to both data and workload. One dataset and one component class; no production-distribution validation reported.

title: MemoriesDB: A Temporal-Semantic-Relational Database for Long-Term Agent Memory / Modeling Experience as a Graph of Temporal-Semantic Surfaces
review_status: full-text audit complete; prototype design reviewed; paper labels performance table illustrative rather than formal benchmark and reports no formal coherence metric
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2025-11-09; full HTML audited
evidence_note: The paper calls its insert/throughput table illustrative estimates, not formal benchmarking; its implementation is for feasibility rather than competition with optimized engines, no formal coherence metrics are reported, and agent-behavior validation is future work. Limitations include embedding-distribution drift, deletion/privacy issues, and vector-dimension query cost.

title: DSB: A Decision Support Benchmark for Workload-Driven and Traditional Database Systems
review_status: citation-follow-up primary-source check complete; prior-art counterexample to any claim that configurable/dynamic database workloads did not exist before DriftBench
sections_checked: scope of TPC-DS-derived data/query extensions and configurable/dynamic workloads
evidence_note: The primary paper and Microsoft Research description document DSB as an open-source TPC-DS-derived benchmark with more complex distributions/query templates and configurable/dynamic workloads. This narrows DriftBench's potential novelty to schema-driven composition of data, query, and temporal drift; DSB is a counterexample to a blanket absence-of-dynamic-benchmarks claim, but may not cover the same schema and drift dimensions.
